It's extremely rare that it can be 100% proven that somebody broke the law (Usually that requires a video explicitly displaying the crime). That's basically a myth perpetuated by TV and hollywood (CSI and whatnot) - Most of the time it's deductive reasoning using the evidence available. This is why people have to deal with having a lawyer instead of just representing themselves. Lawyers know the grounds on which evidence is considered permissible and try to basically get all of the opposing evidence thrown out while keeping all of yours intact. This is why almost every lawyer will tell you (if you end up in custody) never, ever talk to the police (The Miranda rights are explicit about anything you say or do can be used AGAINST you in the court of law, but they can't actually be used as evidence FOR you). A grand majority of such cases are resolved before they even get to court by the police soliciting written or verbal confessions from people. It doesn't actually prove that they did it because in many cases they were basically tricked into bearing witness against themselves, but it secures a guilty sentencing.
